methods.name: Peer-Median

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Mitra Chem is a Series B climate and energy technology company founded by Vivas Kumar and Will Chueh that has raised $60M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private frontier-tech companies and 1 public peer (Linamar, ticker LNZA) operating in the same sector and stage cohort, including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Redwood Materials, and QuantumScape.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $60M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage progression, yielding $114M. Peer-median analysis examines three directly comparable same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies: KoBold Metals ($3.0B Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B Series C), and Amogy ($700M Series C). The median valuation across this peer set is $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B. These two methods produce materially different outputs, reflecting inherent stage and maturity dispersion within the peer set.

Triangulating these approaches yields a range of $97M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $557M. The wide dispersion reflects uncertainty around (1) revenue trajectory and commercialization timing relative to later-stage peers, and (2) appropriate stage-adjusted discount from Series C valuations. Additional sensitivity to technology risk and capital efficiency would narrow confidence intervals.
